## The column state and its configuration (`AtmState2D`, `CoreConfig`) {#sec-ch09-state}

### Summary

The two-dimensional solver works on a grid of columns: a vertical coordinate $x_1$ with `nlyr` cells and a
horizontal coordinate $x_2$ with `ncol` cells. Each cell holds a temperature, a pressure and the concentration of
every species. `AtmState2D` stores these as tensors and derives the cell centres and spacings once, so every operator
of this chapter reads its geometry from one place. A small configuration object chooses the transport form and the
chemistry solver.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Hold the cell-centred state on an `(ncol, nlyr)` grid and its geometry.

**Data.** Faces `x1f` (`nlyr`+1), `x2f` (`ncol`+1); $T$, $p$ `(ncol, nlyr)`; concentrations `(ncol, nlyr, nspecies)`.

**Placement.** Built by the caller; passed to every operator, step and source of this chapter.

**Activation.** API: `AtmState2D(x1f, x2f, temperature, pressure, concentration, gravity)`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Shapes checked at construction; units are the caller's (see Limits).

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $x_{1,i}$, $x_{2,j}$, cell-centre coordinates; $x_{1,i\pm1/2}$, face coordinates;
$\Delta x_{1,i} = x_{1,i+1/2} - x_{1,i-1/2}$, cell width; $\delta x_{1,i+1/2} = x_{1,i+1} - x_{1,i}$, distance between
adjacent centres; $c_{j,i,n}$, concentration of species $n$ in column $j$, layer $i$.

### Derivation

The geometry is defined from the face coordinates alone:

$$
\begin{aligned}
x_{1,i} &= \tfrac12\left(x_{1,i-1/2} + x_{1,i+1/2}\right), \\
\Delta x_{1,i} &= x_{1,i+1/2} - x_{1,i-1/2}, \\
\delta x_{1,i+1/2} &= x_{1,i+1} - x_{1,i},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-state-geometry}

and the same for $x_2$. @eq-ch09-state-geometry is computed in `__post_init__`
({{< code python/atm2d/atm_state2d.py AtmState2D.__post_init__ >}}). Face temperatures used by binary diffusion are
the arithmetic mean of the two adjacent cells (`temperature_x1f`). Nothing here is approximate: the centres are
midpoints by definition, and every operator of this chapter uses exactly these spacings.

### Numerical method

No numerical method. `x1` is vertical and `x2` horizontal, and the state tensors are laid out `(ncol, nlyr, ...)`
with the species last; the flattened index of `(column, layer, species)` used by the sparse system is
`(column * nlyr + layer) * nspecies + species` (`flatten_state_index`, @sec-ch09-assembly).

Boundary conditions are given per side in `SpeciesBoundaryConditions2D`: `left` and `right` are the first and last
columns ($x_2$ ends), `bottom` and `top` the first and last layers ($x_1$ ends). At a corner cell two sides apply;
`left` and `right` are applied first and then overwritten by `bottom` and `top`, so a corner takes the bottom or top
condition ({{< code python/atm2d/transport.py _apply_boundary_conditions >}}; the row forms are in the Numerical
method of @sec-ch09-transport).

The transport form and the chemistry solver are chosen by `CoreConfig`
({{< code python/atm2d/config.py CoreConfig >}}): `transport_form` (`c_diffusion`, `mr_diffusion`, `mr_exp`,
`mr_hybrid`, or `None` for the density-dependent default of @sec-ch09-transport) and `chem_solver` (`newton`, `bdf`,
`lsoda`, `radau`). Unless a caller installs one with `set_core_config`, `get_core_config` reads them from the
environment variables `KINTERA_TRANSPORT_FORM` and `KINTERA_CHEM_SOLVER` at every call.

The state figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

| active configuration | {{< code python/atm2d/config.py get_core_config >}} | `get_core_config` | environment |

: Code map of the state and configuration. {#tbl-ch09-state-code}

Setup checks a user can hit: faces that are not one-dimensional or have fewer than two entries; a temperature or
pressure not shaped `(ncol, nlyr)`; concentrations not shaped `(ncol, nlyr, nspecies)`; a boundary-kind list whose
length is not `nspecies`; boundary values not broadcastable to `(nedge, nspecies)`.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_atm2d.py` | every operator test builds its state through `AtmState2D` | n/a | construction |

: Tests of the state. {#tbl-ch09-state-tests}

No test checks the geometry of @eq-ch09-state-geometry on its own; it is exercised by the transport tests of
@sec-ch09-transport. `test_atm2d.py` is registered with ctest at the pin.

### Limits

The state carries no units. The default `gravity` is 980.665, a value in cm s$^{-2}$ (CGS), and the binary-diffusion
operator uses a gas constant in CGS units (`GAS_CONSTANT_CGS` in `transport.py`), while the rest of kintera is SI
(verified by reading). A caller mixing SI state with the binary-diffusion operator must convert; that a mismatch
gives silently wrong diffusion rates is a hypothesis, not run. The configuration is read from the environment at every
call unless one is installed, so changing an environment variable between two calls changes the transport form.
